claimBoundary: This is a deliberately stopped diagnostic, not a completed course, a benchmark score, an adapter win, or promotion evidence. No result from this run may be inherited by a later candidate or paired comparison.

findings.detail: Each of the six base synthesis requests consumed three native generations polishing quiz and key-term fields, although the staged adapter would replace those fields and needed only a structurally usable fact draft.

The browser protocol requested one exact source-grounded attempt, while the local benchmark server silently used up to three. Four completed adapter stages therefore consumed 3, 1, 2, and 3 native generations.

The candidate arm had already consumed 38 native generations behind 21 transport requests before one course completed. Continuing would measure a retry-policy mismatch rather than the staged adapter architecture intended for production.

resolution.factsFirstSynthesis: When the route receipt proves an exact source-grounded adapter stage is available, base synthesis stops after its first structurally usable, fact-valid draft.
resolution.singleAdapterAttempt: The exact source-grounded stage receives one native generation in both browser and local benchmark transports; failed adapter output falls back to the base draft plus deterministic compiler repair.
resolution.scopeGuard: Only an exact source-grounded adapter manifest can activate the shortcut. Unrelated, legacy, invalid, or prompt-mismatched adapters retain the existing bounded retry policy.
resolution.nextEvidence: A fresh clean-tree V11 run must start from zero and complete both paired arms before any efficiency, quality, or promotion claim.
